subject: Dedicated reservation options & activation worksheet - Tethys AI
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@tethys.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Draft dedicated reservation options & activation worksheet (first pass)

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Per our conversation I put together three differentiated reservation options for Tethys AI that balance predictability and runway flexibility. Attached is a short PDF and an activation worksheet (xlsx) that shows month-by-month GPU counts and an estimated token cost burn for the first 12 months. High-level options:

- Option A (Conservative): 24 GPUs dedicated (baseline), soft-burst credits, 2-month warmup window. Fastest path to SLA but higher unit cost.
- Option B (Balanced): 12 GPUs baseline, auto-burst up to 36 for peak windows, 3-month ramp (12 -> 24 -> 36). Lower monthly commit, built-in burst/CSP for spikes.
- Option C (Phased Onramp): 6 GPUs baseline with reserved growth credits to reach 30 GPUs over 9 months; includes model-quantization consultation + 8 weeks of prewarm credits. Lowest initial commitment, longer time to full throughput.

A few notes we discussed: minimums matter for concurrency (we reserve GPU lanes to guarantee throughput), and your inference mix (many short chat calls vs. long-context generations) changes the projection in the worksheet. Karthik can run a quick model-profile pass on your sample traces if you share them; that will let us tighten the cost projection.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the PDF and worksheet — mark up the months where you expect marketing/launch spikes.
2) If you’re comfortable, pick 1 preferred option + 1 fallback.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-minute alignment with SRE/CS to lock SLA targets and handover schedule.

I left the contract cadence flexible (monthly billing on committed GPU hours, plus a smoothing credit for month-over-month ramp). If you want, we can convert Option B into a stepped commitment (e.g., 12 for months 1–3, 24 for months 4–8, 36 thereafter) — I included a worked example in the worksheet.

Thanks —
Marcus

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the worksheet. A couple quick clarifying questions before we loop in finance and our infra leads: 

1) For Option B (the balanced one) — when you say "auto-burst up to 36" can you clarify billing during burst? Is burst billed at a higher per-hour rate or consumed from a pre-purchased burst credit pool?
2) For Option C — curious what the SLA looks like at 6 GPUs baseline. Our product team expects 95th percentile latency targets that are tight during peak sessions.
3) Can you share the assumptions you used for average tokens per request and tokens/sec? We want to compare with our internal profiler.

Also, our procurement team prefers a single-year commitment if possible; they asked for options that show a 12-month effective blended price per GPU-hour.

Regards,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@tethys.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T11:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft dedicated reservation options & activation worksheet (first pass)

Rajesh —

Quick answers inline and I attached a small extract of the profiling assumptions I used to compute the worksheet:

1) Burst billing: we do two modes. For soft-burst (Option A) we bill at committed rate but you receive burst-credits (hours) that are priced into the commitment (effectively smoothing the per-hour). For auto-burst (Option B) we implement a hybrid: bursts draw from an on-demand pool billed at a modest uplift (~15%) unless you consume purchased burst credits. The worksheet shows both a "credits" and an "on-demand uplift" path for months with heavy spikes.

2) 6 GPUs SLA: at 6 GPUs baseline you will not meet the same latency SLOs for sustained peak concurrency. Short spikes are OK with burst routing but sustained peak will see queuing and increased 95th-percentile. For interactive latency guarantees we recommend a minimum baseline that covers your 95th-percentile concurrent tokens/sec expectation plus a 20% buffer — for your sample traces that maps closer to 18–24 GPUs.

3) Assumptions: average request size 1.6k tokens (inference + prompt), model throughput ~30 tokens/sec per GPU under current quant profile; these are conservative. I can run a more optimistic quant-run if you plan to use int8/4-bit.

If helpful, I can run a quick three-scenario sim (current traces) and paste results into the worksheet; that will show expected latency tail and monthly burn for each option.

-karthik

From: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@tethys.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft dedicated reservation options & activation worksheet (first pass)

Thanks Karthik — that helps. We ran the worksheet quickly with our local profiler and the numbers look consistent with your conservative assumptions. A couple of action items from our side:

- We can currently commit to a stepped path similar to your suggested stepped Option B: 12 GPUs (months 1–3) -> 24 GPUs (months 4–7) -> 36 GPUs (months 8–12) if the blended 12-month rate comes in within 8% of our target.
- We'll need RD to validate that 12->24 switching window has a clear activation SLA (how long from notice until GPUs are active and any prewarm latency expectations).
- Procurement asked for a simple 12-month blended price and a short appendix showing crash-recovery playbook and fallbacks. Can you include the fallback lane that routes traffic to hosted GPUs (with a different token price) if Dedicated becomes saturated?

I'll get our procurement contact Priya Shah on the thread for formal pricing.

Rajesh

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Menon <rajesh@tethys.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@tethys.ai>

Date: 2026-11-20T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft dedicated reservation options & activation worksheet (first pass)

Hi Rajesh / Priya —

Appreciate the confirmation and the willingness to proceed with a stepped Option B. Attached is an updated PDF with:
- A 12-month blended price table (shows both committed-only and committed+burst-credit blended lines).
- Activation SLA: our standard is 72-hour activation for stepped increases up to 2x baseline and 7-day for larger moves; we will include a one-time prewarm window (48 hours of free GPU warm-up) during the first major step.
- Fallback lane: we documented a routed fallback to our hosted pool (region us-west), which is automatically invoked if queueing exceeds thresholds for >15 minutes. Fallback is billed at hosted rates + 25% uplift; we include automatic throttling rules to protect SLAs during failover.

Action items I will own this week:
1) Finalize the blended 12-month pricing with finance and post in the worksheet (Deliverable: updated xlsx).
2) Draft a short appendix for crash-recovery playbook and hand off to Grace for CS sign-off.
3) Prepare a simple amendment (1 page) that Priya can feed into procurement showing step schedule, activation SLA, and termination terms.

I’ll target sending the finalized worksheet and amendment by EOD Friday next week. If you want to accelerate, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the procurement team through the construct.

Best —
Marcus
